clue.text: Unfashionable London suburb's flanked by the main town in Essex

indicators.note: to be flanked by something is to have it on both sides, so the sea word wraps around the rest

parts.note: the main is an old poetic name for the open sea
something unfashionable is out of fashion, simply out
Hendon is a suburb of north London, with the possessive S kept

explanation.surface: A sniffy put-down: some unfashionable suburb is bracketed with the chief town of Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the open sea in old poetry. Southend-on-Sea is a seaside town on the Thames estuary in Essex; Hendon is a north London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a large seaside resort on the north bank of the Thames estuary, in the county of Essex.

clue.text: What might lead to disease where you might get crabs?

parts.note: read the two words of the answer as wordplay: the first word, ... (rearranged), spells the clue's word disease

explanation.surface: A smutty question about catching crabs, the louse, which turns innocent once you think of the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, taken as an instruction, rearranges its first word into 'disease'. 'Crabs' hints at an unpleasant infestation, but here they are the shellfish in rock pools.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs scuttle about on beaches and rock pools at coastal holiday towns, so that is where a child might catch them.

clue.text: How 8 20 is rated, commonly third out of four

definitions.text: How 8 20 is rated, commonly third out of four

parts.words: How 8 20 is rated, commonly third out of four
parts.note: the film Summer Holiday carries the British U certificate, and U is the third letter of the word four

explanation.surface: A film buff's note on the rating of a classic, with a puzzling aside about ranking third of four.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 20 is the cross-reference to the film at 8 and 20 Down. British film certificates mark family films U, the abbreviation in common use; U is also the third letter of 'four'.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Board of Film Classification's U rating stands for this word, marking a film suitable for all audiences.

clue.text: Accommodation in the middle of Southport

definitions.text: Accommodation in the middle of Southport

parts.words: Accommodation in the middle of Southport
parts.note: the central letter of the nine-letter word Southport is H, and the NATO phonetic alphabet's word for H is also a place to stay

explanation.surface: A guide-book line: lodging in the centre of the Lancashire seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of SOUTHPORT is H, and radio operators spell H with this code word. Southport is a seaside resort in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a building providing rooms for travellers to sleep in, a kind of lodging, and also the radio code word for the letter H.

clue.text: As a rule, even choice of enemy has friend's support

indicators.note: of links the choice to the picked letters, putting the alternative word between them
even says to take the second and fourth letters of the word enemy

parts.note: a choice is an alternative, signalled by the word or
an ally is a friend, placed beneath as support in this down entry

explanation.surface: A sort of proverb: as a rule, even when you pick an enemy, a friend will back you up.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'even choice of enemy' as a choice between the even letters of 'enemy', written N-or-M. 'Has' and 'support' set the friend underneath in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally and as a rule both mean usually, in the ordinary run of things.

clue.text: Working phone available if required

parts.note: a machine that is working is switched on
to phone someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A description of a mobile that is switched on so its owner can be reached when needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who is on call can be summoned at any time, ready to work when needed.

clue.text: Four bards surprised what's for hire in Newquay

indicators.note: surprised suggests being thrown into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Four poets are startled by something on offer in a Cornish holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newquay is a resort on the north coast of Cornwall, England's best-known surfing town.
explanation.definitionFit: Newquay's beaches draw surfers, and the shops there rent out the board you ride the waves on.

clue.text: Article on books: 39 books for Protestant religious leader

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
B is short for book, doubled for the plural as pp is for pages
the Protestant Old Testament has thirty-nine books, abbreviated OT

explanation.surface: A theological puzzle: an article about books and the Protestant canon, written for a church leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Protestant Bibles count 39 books in the Old Testament, against 46 in Catholic ones, hence the qualifier.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of an abbey of monks, a religious leader in the monastic sense.

clue.text: Film showing body of water in France during broadcast ad break

indicators.note: during means happening within, so the French sea sits inside the rest

parts.note: the word ad spoken sounds like add, and to add is to sum
a break from work is a holiday
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A TV schedule note: a film about a French lake shown during the commercials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' signals the sound: AD heard is 'add', which gives SUM. Summer Holiday is the 1963 Cliff Richard musical about a bus trip across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a classic British musical film starring Cliff Richard, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: A Johnson, perhaps, that's advanced through backing bullshit

parts.note: via means by way of, through

indicators.note: backing means the word that follows is reversed

parts.note: rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: A political jibe: a Johnson (Boris, we think) who got ahead thanks to talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Boris Johnson; the Johnson meant is Amy Johnson, the pioneering 1930s pilot who flew solo from England to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy Johnson was a famous pilot, so a Johnson is one example of a person who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Initially Cupid annoyed Rudolph, in being one uppity reindeer

indicators.note: initially says to take the opening letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Santa's team squabbles: Cupid gets cross with Rudolph for being stuck up.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribou is the North American name for the same deer species that Europeans call reindeer.

clue.text: One young chap making comeback after catching last appearance of George Best

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: catching means taking something inside
a comeback is a return, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a lad is a young chap

indicators.note: the last appearance of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A footballing tale: a youngster's comeback, after he caught George Best's final game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like part of George Best, the Manchester United footballer, but it is the definition. LAD catching E gives LAED, reversed to DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal is the best possible, the perfect choice.

clue.text: Without preparation, built amid disorder?

indicators.note: disorder says the letters are thrown into confusion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something put up in chaos, with no planning at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad libitum is Latin for at pleasure; to ad lib is to speak or play off the cuff, unrehearsed.

clue.text: Group sense I'm able when wanting leaders

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so each word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A member of a band feels capable only when nobody is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letters of SENSE, I'M and ABLE leaves ENSE, M and BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a group of musicians or performers working together.

clue.text: Male bowler, for one brief time on an island

parts.note: a man is a male
a bowler is an example of a hat
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A cricketer, a male bowler, spends a short spell on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket but is the round hard felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of New York City sits on an island between the Hudson and East rivers.

clue.text: Foil for food container?

definitions.meaning: to foil is to frustrate or impede someone
a wicker basket for a picnic or Christmas food parcel

explanation.surface: Kitchen talk: is foil a wrapping for something you keep food in?
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper someone is to hinder them; a hamper is also a lidded basket packed with food.

clue.text: What shows costs involved in Cecil's leaderless trip?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together
leaderless means the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: An expenses question about a jaunt taken by someone called Cecil, minus the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' drops C from CECIL'S to leave ECILS; 'involved' then mixes ECILS with TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A price list is a table setting out what each item costs.

clue.text: Jacob's son died, with collar showing one sign of dermatitis

parts.note: Dan was one of the twelve sons of Jacob in Genesis
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies
a ruff is a frilled Elizabethan collar

explanation.surface: A biblical figure's death and his fancy collar, which turns out to bear a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaking scalp skin is a common symptom of seborrhoeic dermatitis, so it signals the condition.

clue.text: Change your mind about period of abstinence

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Lent is the forty days before Easter when Christians give things up

explanation.surface: Someone wavers over giving something up for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and give way, abandoning a harsh decision.

clue.text: See 1
With German setter on beach briefly, somewhere in Kent

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means following what comes before
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: sands are a beach
ich is German for I, the setter of the crossword

explanation.surface: A setter goes to the beach with a German friend, somewhere in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' suggests a dog but means the crossword setter, I, in German. Sandwich is a historic town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandwich is a town in Kent, one of the medieval Cinque Ports, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: See 8
Made annoying noise when out in sun, mostly now showing one's been out in it too long?

parts.note: S is short for sun, as in Sunday

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.words: showing one's been out in it too long
parts.note: skin goes red with sunburn after too long in the sun

explanation.surface: A sunbather out cold on the beach, sounding off and turning pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' means asleep here; the second 'out' means out in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out is fast asleep, and a sleeper who snored made a noisy breathing sound.

clue.text: Bronzed swimming nudes include model girl?

indicators.note: include means holding the other letters inside
swimming suggests movement and confusion, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Skinny-dippers who have brought along a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' gives SUNED from the nudes, and 'include' has it take in the model and the girl. Model T was Henry Ford's famous car.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronzed skin has turned a golden brown in the sun.

clue.text: Things required if hooligans take Ecstasy

indicators.note: take means swallowing something, holding it inside

parts.note: neds is Scottish slang for young hooligans
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug warning: what follows if yobs pop pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' sounds like taking a drug but means NEDS takes E in.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are necessities, the things a person must have.

clue.text: Native American large basket

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada and the northern US
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big woven basket made by a Native American craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket used by anglers to carry their catch.

clue.text: Round collar

definitions.meaning: a round song, sung by several voices entering in turn
to collar is to arrest or grab someone

explanation.surface: A shirt-maker's description of a circular neckband.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a type of round for voices; to catch a suspect is to collar them.

clue.text: Once again insert some green terminology

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An editor tells you to put back some environmentalist jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter data is to type or put it in a second time.

clue.text: New Tinder user primarily, so not yet experienced

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A newcomer to a dating app is inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Untried means not yet tested or put to the proof.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical council spelt out why nobody's fit

indicators.note: spelt out suggests the letters are laid out afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: A church meeting explains why none of its members is up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: The Synod of Whitby in 664 was a church council that settled the date of Easter for Northumbria.
